title: School board announces RIFs
description: After a special meeting of the Custer School District (CSD) Board of Education April 7 in Custer, a reduction in force was announced. In total, the reduction in force will include nine classified positions of general education paraprofessionals, library aides and office assistants, three certified positions and three-and-a half custodial/maintenance positions. For the most part, this is being addressed through attrition.

title: Commission hears of dwindling reserves
description: Custer County’s cash reserves are slowly dwindling, and if every department within the county spent the entirety of its budget, the county would be financially strapped. That was the message given by county finance officer Dawn McLaughlin at the April 8 meeting of the Custer County Commission, as McLaughlin walked those in the crowd through the county’s past, present and future budget situation.

title: Turning Point USA Faith hub launching
description: A new Turning Point (TP) USA Faith hub is launching in the Southern Hills, including Hill City, Keystone, Custer County and Fall River County. The project is being undertaken by a group of community leaders and spearheaded by third-generation Custer resident Pat Baumann.

title: Fire burns over 5,000 east county acres
description: A rapidly-spreading fire on the eastern side of Custer County torched 5,408 acres last weekend before forward progress on the fire was stopped. The 79 Fire three miles north of Buffalo Gap was reported around 11:35 a.m. on Saturday, April 11. According to the South Dakota Department of Public Safety, it started just east of Hwy. 79 along East French Creek Road in eastern Custer County. State, federal and local resources along with air support were on initial attack of the fire, which burned primarily grass.

title: City council gets update on West Dam progress
description: The second phase of construction on West Dam is winding down and the third phase is in high gear, it was learned at the April 6 meeting of the Custer City Council. Steve Bareis of RESPEC Engineering, one of the firms helping the city through the project, was present at the meeting via video conferencing and walked the council and those in attendance through a slide show of the work that has been completed and the work that is ongoing. The second phase, which is removal of material from the reservoir and embankment excavation, is expected to be wrapped up by early May.

title: 87 Fire
description: Firefighters responded to the five-acre 87 Fire located approximately four miles south of Hill City off of Hwy. 87 (Needles Highway) April 10. Aircraft, including helicopters, an air attack platform and two single engine air tankers worked the fire along with federal, state and local resources. Forward progress was stopped with dozer lines and hose lay around the fire. Firefighters staffed the fire overnight.

title: Huge change for residential neighborhoods discussed
County suspends search for missing Hill City man
Former lodge facing tax deed action
Environmental, tribal concerns persist as fireworks bring ‘rock concert in phone booth’ to Mount Rushmore
Off to the races for 2026 elections
description: Petitions are in, and the results are out. While several town board and city council seats were open across the county, there will only be an election for the Hermosa and Buffalo Gap town boards. The rest did not receive enough petitions to warrant an election. However, the Custer and Elk Mountain School Districts will see an election. The Custer County Commissioner role has the most candidates, and there will be District 30 races this election as well.

title: County enacts hiring freeze
description: Custer County is staring at a potential budget crisis down the road if it doesn’t act now to cut spending. That is the position of at least two Custer County Commission members who have spent several weeks studying the issue, it was revealed at the March 25 meeting of the commission.

title: Water could be next on tap for city
description: With its renovated/upgraded wastewater system set to go online in a couple of months, the City of Custer will likely now focus—at least sometime in the near future—on an upgrade to the entrance on the opposite side of the water system.

title: Commission OKs abatements
description: A property tax/abatement issue that began last November came to a conclusion at the March 25 meeting of the Custer County Commission, as the commission agreed to a full abatement on a pair of Custer County lots while agreeing to split the difference on a requested abatement on six other lots. All told, the county abated $24,147.71 in property taxes for which it has sent out bills.

title: Legislators proud of property tax relief
Petition results for 2026 election
Towns tests over the limit on forever chemicals
Black Hills Energy seeks rate increase
description: By Jason Ferguson

title: Custer County churches celebrate Holy Week
description: Custer County churches are celebrating Holy Week with a number of special services. This year, Maundy Thursday is April 2, Good Friday is April 3 and Easter Sunday is April 5. Custer Lutheran Fellowship ELCA is having a Maundy Thursday service at 6:30 p.m and a Good Friday Crosswalk at 6:30 p.m. Then, an Easter Sunrise Worship service will take place at 6:30 a.m., followed by a worship service at 9:30 a.m.

title: Ad hoc group says ‘more T-shirts needed’ in Custer
description: By Jason Ferguson

title: Community response to Qury Fire ‘impressive’
description: In the aftermath of the Qury Fire, which began March 12, many are marveling at the community’s response to the incident, from providing meals and lodging for evacuees to volunteering hours of time to help emergency services. “Having people and organizations step up like that, it makes the job very rewarding,” said Custer County Emergency Management director Steve Esser. “I can’t say enough about how great it was to have so many people that were a part of how successful it was.”

title: Sheriff’s office talks patrol changes
description: When the City of Custer opted not to enter into a law enforcement contract with   Custer County for law enforcement services within the city, it not only trimmed the county’s law enforcement budget by over $300,000, but it also changed the way the sheriff’s office patrolled the county, county officials say. The results of that change were discussed at the March 11 meeting of the Custer County Commission.

title: Drainfields a hot topic at county meeting
description: Under the road or over the section line? That was the dilemma facing the Custer County Commission at its March 11 meeting. The issue came when Alex Heim told the commission he had a failing drainfield at his VIP Road home. To install a new drainfield he will either need to put a new wastewater pipe under VIP road—to property he owns on the other side of the road for a spot to build a new drainfield—or cross a section line and run onto his neighbors’ property to build the drainfield.

title: Noe promoted, Ferguson demoted
description: Southern Hills Publishing general manager Jason Ferguson has announced the promotion of Esther Noe to general manager, while subsequently announcing he has demoted himself to “door- opening associate,” which he described as being similar to a Wal-Mart greeter only less cheerful and sans a blue vest. Perhaps a toga, he said.

title: Task order change denied
Rebranding on the way for Hill City
EDC tries to solve affordable housing puzzle
New Underwood wildland fire
description: The New Underwood Volunteer Fire Department responded to a report of a wildland fire in the 22000 block of Sharpe Rd, Unincorporated Pennington County. Upon arrival firefighters observed a wind-driven fire burning in cured vegetation under critical fire weather conditions and immediately struck a second alarm. The fire threatened infrastructure, and caused damage to ranching assets. Firefighters contained the fire to approximately 43 acres. No injuries to firefighters, civilians, livestock or domestic animals were reported.

title: Coyote Flats Fire hits Rockerville
State opens 40 more slots in teacher  apprenticeship program
Qury’s final tally is 9,168 acres
description: Eleven days after it started, the Qury Fire Type 3 Interagency Incident Management Team transitioned management of the fire to a Type 4 operation.

title: Hermosa still rife with controversy
description: Between alleged open meeting violations, long an issue in Hermosa, routinely four-hour-long board meetings, publicly scrutinized financial decisions, the revolving door of board chairmanship and the firing and hiring of legal counsel, the Hermosa Board of Trustees has been fraught with contention and near-upheaval for years, and that has not changed in recent weeks and months.

title: School district talks staff attrition
description: The Custer School District (CSD) is looking at implementing attrition and restructuring methods to improve efficiency and decrease costs in the district. Ultimately, the goal is to balance the district’s annual budget while continuing to provide a great education for students. “Attrition is the key to all the changes that we’re trying to make,” said superintendent of schools Dr. Tim Frederick. “It’s trying to become more efficient and more effective with the resources that we have and that we can continue to keep for sustainability for the district going forward.”

title: Harlow’s allegations discussed at Hill City meeting
description: Several people attended the most recent Hill City School District Board of Education meeting to discuss safety concerns involving Harlow’s School Bus Service and the resignation of several drivers in the previous weeks. During the audience with individuals portion of the meeting, Kelli Werlinger, the new location manager for Harlow’s, addressed the board. “I’m sure you’ve noticed there’s been quite a few changes with services the last few weeks,” she began, going on to discuss the driver walk-out that affected both Hill City and Custer services.

title: Fire opt-out rationale given
description: Custer County volunteer fire departments are on borrowed time—literally and figuratively. That was the message delivered at a special March 9 public meeting held to allow the public to hear what local firefighters say are the reasons for a proposed tax opt-out that will be on the June ballot. If approved, the opt-out will allow the county to opt out of its current fire fund tax levy to raise more funds for county fire departments that are not already within a taxing district.

title: Fanned by wind and dry conditions, Qury Fire consumes over 9,000 acres
description: Fire season has come to Custer County, and it’s only the middle of March. A day that started with a Red Flag warning ended in disaster in Custer County Thursday, March 12, when a pair of fires broke out off Hazelrodt Cutoff two miles southeast of Custer that afternoon. Aided by strong winds and dry conditions the fires merged and has so far chewed up 9,059 acres of Custer County land before being mostly corraled by hundreds of firefighters who converged on Custer from local, state and federal agencies. The fire began just after 1 p.m. last Thursday.

title: School resource officer contract approved
description: The Custer School District (CSD) has arranged a two-year contract with the Custer County Sheriff’s Office for a School Resource Officer (SRO) at $65,000 per year. Further details were discussed at the Board of Education March 9 at the Custer board room. Board vice president Travis Hartshorn, board member Heath Reindl and superintendent of schools Dr. Tim Frederick met with the Custer County Commission to discuss the situation and worked out a plan to keep an SRO in the district.

title: Firework lottery dates released
Free bridge not so free anymore
Bus concerns addressed at school board meeting
Emergency closure order issued for Qury Fire
Qury fire now over 7,200 acres
description: The Qury Fire, which is now listed at 7,200a cres, has claimed structures on 10 properties, it was reported last evening during a special community forum regarding the fire held at the Custer Jr./Sr. High School Theater. Custer County Sheriff's Office Lt. Derrick Reifenrath told the assembled crowd that structures lost varied from outbuildings and garages to homes. He did not say how many homes were lost.

title: Ongoing tap talk transpires in Keystone
French Creek lawsuit dismissed
description: A federal judge has dismissed a federal lawsuit aimed at preventing the City of Custer from discharging effluent into French Creek, seemingly clearing the path for the City of Custer to begin the discharge nearly a year after reconstruction and renovation work was complete on its wastewater treatment facility.

title: You can be a child’s new TeamMate
description: By dedicating 30 minutes a week, you could change the life of a student in the Custer School District (CSD) through the TeamMates Mentoring Program. The mission of TeamMates is “To positively impact the world by inspiring students to reach their full potential through mentoring.” TeamMates is a mentorship program designed to occur during a school day. Meetings are held at the school, usually during lunch, so the mentee’s academic schedule is not interrupted. In 2018, CSD was the first school in South Dakota to implement the TeamMates program.

title: County sales tax heads to Rhoden’s desk
description: Two bills that would allow local governments to impose new sales taxes for specific purposes cleared their last legislative hurdles on Thursday at the South Dakota Capitol in Pierre and are headed to the governor for his consideration.

title: Food truck presence questioned
description: The presence of a food truck in Custer—even if for only one day—during Custer Restaurant Week had some restaurant owners fit to be tied. At its March 2 meeting the Custer City Council hard from Custer Area Chamber of Commerce director Dawn Murray came before the council to say she had been contacted by restaurant owners to voice displeasure over the presence of the food truck, which spent a day at Custer Ace Hardware during Restaurant Week. Murray asked how the situation could be rectified for the future.

title: Trading property tax for sales tax
USDA approves emergency forest restoration assistance
description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Farm Service Agency (FSA) in Custer/Fall River Counties is accepting applications for the Emergency Forest Restoration Program (EFRP) to address damages from the severe windstorm that occurred Dec. 18. EFRP provides financial cost-share and technical assistance to restore nonindustrial private forestland (NIPF) damaged by a qualifying natural disaster. EFRP signup began Jan. 26 and ends March 27.

title: Family resource fair Saturday
description: This Saturday, March 14, the Custer Elementary School gym will transform into a “one-stop shop” for local parents and caregivers. Early Learner Custer invites the community to the third Annual Southern Hills Family Resource Fair, running from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. This free community event is specifically designed for families with children ages 0–8. It aims to bridge the gap between Southern Hills families and the essential services that help children thrive, from prenatal development through the early elementary years.

title: Carnival coming to CHS prom April 25
description: It’s going to be a night of fun, dancing and celebrating at Custer High School prom Saturday, April 25. This year’s theme is “Rio Carnival,” and attendees can expect an abundance of vibrant, leafy, colorful decorations, including some feathers and balloons. Students should plan to arrive at school around 6 p.m. to pay for their tickets, take some pictures with friends and family members and prepare to line up for the grand march. Tickets are $15 each.

title: Fire opt-out on June 2 ballot
description: Voters in a large swath of Custer County will head to the polls June 2 to decide if they want to supply more money to local volunteer fire departments that are not already part of a taxing district. The vote will affect voters in every corner of the county, save for those located within the boundaries of the Battle Creek Fire District and the Fairburn Fire District, both of which already have formed their own taxing jurisdictions to collect their own revenue  apart from the county levy.

title: New ELA curriculum recommended for school
description: Members of the Custer School District literacy/curriculum development team, including Jacqueline Hagen, Conni Virtue, Hallie Webster and Jenn Doyle, presented their process and recommendation for the next English Language Arts (ELA) curriculum at the board of education meeting April 13 in Hermosa. The literacy/curriculum development team consists of teachers and administrators from Custer and Hermosa. Doyle said it started by partnering with Compass, but realized it could achieve the same thing independently more efficiently and effectively while saving the district money.

title: Town attorney, engineer in crosshairs
description: There was a time last year when citizens were attending Hermosa Board of Trustee meetings with their own popcorn, and after the four-hour April 7 regular meeting, some wondered if that should be revisited. When the agenda for this meeting was published the week prior, there was an item for approving a budget to hire a new town attorney.

title: Lessons learned from Qury Fire
description: Custer County is full of well-trained first responders who are ready to answer the call during an emergency at a moment’s notice. That doesn’t mean there aren’t lessons to be learned in the aftermath of an emergency. Such is the case now over a month removed from the Qury Fire, the fast-moving blaze that burned over 9,000 acres of land a little over two miles southeast of the City of Custer.

title: French Creek flood mitigation site up
description: In 2019, severe rainfall led to flash flooding along French Creek, sending water into streets, homes and businesses through the City of Custer. The event caused widespread disruptions and highlighted how quickly conditions along the creek can become hazardous.

title: Aldermen table proposal, discuss projects
Keystone asking for compound meter
Business manager Cassandra Ott recognized
Body of missing man found
Take it for ‘grant’ed
South Dakota Wildland Fire unveils new mascot
Prevailer to host Hill City candidate forum May 12
Early voting begins in some South Dakota counties after delay
Voters to determine east Custer ambulance
description: Voters on the eastern side of Custer County will head to the polls June 2 to decide whether or not to pay extra taxes to ensure ambulance coverage continues on that side of the county. For the past several months the Custer County Commission has been working with Pennington County, the Rapid City Fire Department and representatives of the eastern side of the county to bring about the vote, if which approved will bring about the creation of the East Custer Ambulance District.

title: Dakota Cowboy Inn given new life as apartments
description: Many times when someone purchases a building, they give it a facelift. As for the Ponderosa Apartments? It received a facelift, triple bypass, appendectomy, heart transplant and facial reconstruction. Yes, the property formerly known as the Dakota Cowboy Inn needed a little more than a fresh coat of paint. Luckily, Tom Iverson and Daniela Malcoci of Link Investment Group were up to the challenge.

title: City aid sought by HFH
description: Black Hills Area Habitat for Humanity wants to build some affordable workforce housing on north 7th Street in Custer. But it will require some help. That was the message delivered to the Custer City Council at the council’s April 20 meeting. Gene Fennell, a volunteer representative for Black Hills Area Habitat for Humanity, along with organization members Mike Keegan and Scott Engmann came before the council to discuss the issue, asking for the city’s help in solving a utility issue that exists on lots that could be used for Habitat housing.

title: Resident upset with social media posts
description: A Custer County Commission member’s recent conduct on social media was unprofessional, according to a Custer County resident who spoke during the public comment portion of the April 22 meeting of the commission. Becky Treloar said after someone posted information about a Custer County Commission candidate on a public Custer community page, attempts to correct misinformation on the post was followed by what she said was unprofessional conduct by commissioner Mike Busskohl.

title: Hill City moves forward with merchandise ordinance
Prevailer stacks up SDNA awards
Groups unite to protect sacred site
Neighbors band together over horse permit
Commission discusses term limits
description: Should Custer County Commissioners have term limits? Like anything, it depends on who you ask. The question was raised, however, at the April 22 meeting of the commission—by commissioner Craig Hindle—who said he had it added to the agenda because he does not believe anyone should be a lifelong politician, and he had heard from other people on the issue. “I’d like to see where we want to go for this,” he said. “I’d like to see it on the November election and let the taxpayers decide.”

title: Open meetings law violated in Hermosa
description: In Hermosa The complaint about the April 22, 2025 Hermosa Town Board meeting filed by former board member Vicki Henrichsen was forwarded to Custer County State’s Attorney Tracy Kelley, who wrote to the state’s Open Meetings Commission. She believed the town board had violated the law at that April 22 meeting. Kelley said she was unable to substantiate similar violations alleged at July 14 and July 19 meetings for that year. The complaint and documents can be found at boardsandcommissions.sd.gov

title: Hermosa engineer questions article, comments
description: By Laura Lindblom

title: Former Buffalo Gap official arrested
description: Former Town of Buffalo Gap finance officer Heather Jean Besco, AKA Heather Jean Besco-Clyde, has been indicted by a grand jury on allegations that she stole over $100,000 of town funds during her time as finance officer. Besco has been officially charged in Seventh Judicial Circuit Court for Grand Theft-Embezzlement of Property Received in Trust by Custer County state’s attorney Tracy Kelley. The charge is a Class 3 Felony, punishable by up to 15 years in prison and/or a $30,000 fine.

title: Four vie for two seats in state House of Representatives
description: Four candidates—three Republicans and one Democrat—are vying for a pair of two-year terms to represent District 30 in the South Dakota House of Representatives. Two of the candidates are already serving District 30, while the other two have sought a seat  in the legislature before. Incumbent Republican Tim Goodwin lives north of Three Forks near Sheridan Lake, and has served eight years in the House of Representatives. “They say the Senate is a symphony and the House is a rock concert,” he said. “I”m more of a rock concert type of person.”

title: Commission OKs new trailer court
description: Creation of a new mobile home park south of the City of Custer was approved by the Custer County Commission at its April 22 meeting after some discussion regarding how the road through the park would be declared public. County ordinance lays out parameters for mobile home courts, including how much square-feet there must be for each space, water availability, sewer and parking.

title: State fiscal year tax collections ‘doing well’
description: South Dakota is on track to meet or exceed its revenue estimates by the end of the fiscal year, the Legislature’s lead budget expert said Thursday. The state is about $10 million ahead of its year-to-date target, said Jeff Mehlhaff, chief fiscal analyst for the Legislative Research Council’s. The state fiscal year ends June 30. “We’re doing well on the three big revenue sources,” Mehlhaff told lawmakers Joint Appropriations Committee Thursday, referencing sales tax, contractor’s excise taxes and lottery revenue.

title: 1880 Train sold to WCI
Officials emphasize preparedness
Public urged to show patriotic pride
Pe’ Sla protectors win, drilling plan withdrawn
Hulse, Frye-Mueller vie for District 30 Senate
Four vie for two seats in state House of Representatives
Fifty-two seniors set to graduate May 16
description: School is out for the graduating class of 2026. For one last time, they will congregate in the Custer Armory for the 2026 Custer High School graduation ceremony Saturday, May 16, at 2 p.m. before dispersing into the world and beginning the next chapter of their lives. This year, there are 52 graduates. Samuel Cochran is the valedictorian, and Kylee Ellerton is the salutatorian.

title: Chronicle wins multiple SDNA awards
description: The Custer County Chronicle won 19 awards—including seven first place awards—in its category at the 2025 South Dakota NewsMedia (SDNA) Better News Media Contest held as part of the annual SDNA convention held last week at The Lodge in Deadwood. The Chronicle competed in Division II of the competition, for cities 3,000 to 15,000. Chronicle general manager Jason Ferguson brought home four first-place awards, including the award for Best Headline Writing. “Excellent headline writing. Attention-catching, but also accurate. Great job,” the judges wrote.

title: CSP Open House Weekend starts Friday
description: This weekend, May 15-17, residents and visitors can enjoy free entrance into all South Dakota state parks and recreation areas as part of the South Dakota Game, Fish & Parks’ annual open house weekend. In addition, a number of parks will be hosting special events. Camping fees still apply.

title: Guidance sought on sidewalks rules
description: Should property owners along Park Avenue in the Stone Hill Subdivision be required to install sidewalks as they develop their land? That was the question debated at the May 4 meeting of the Custer City Council before the council ultimately decided to send the issue to a pair of committees for further investigation. The issue was raised by city planner Tessah Behlings, who said she was seeking guidance on the issue because of mixed messaging within city documents.

title: Bringing back the procession of flags
description: “Remember when 50 horseback riders proudly carried the state flags down the streets of Custer during Gold Discovery Days? This unforgettable tradition was once a highlight of our parade, and in honor of America’s 250th Birthday, we want to bring it back in a big way for this year’s Gold Discovery Days Celebration—but we need your help,” said Custer Area Chamber of Commerce executive director Dawn Murray.

title: Four vie for school board seats
description: The Custer School District (CSD) Board of Education has three seats up for election for three-year terms in the June 2 primary. Currently, the seats are held by Travis Hartshorn, Larry Baker and Sara Barrick. Hartshorn, Baker and Barrick all filed petitions, as did Mark Perrenoud. Hartshorn grew up in Custer County and currently lives near Hermosa. He is a farmer, rancher and a business owner.

title: Clock ticking on HVAC
description: It could be tomorrow. It could be in a month. A year. Maybe five years. One thing is certain—the heating and cooling system at the Custer County Courthouse is nearing the end of its useful life. That was the message once again given by county maintenance director Joe Panza at the May 13 meeting of the Custer County Commission.

title: Woman dead after CSP buffalo attack
description: A 70-year-old Canadian woman has died after being charged and thrown by a buffalo in Custer State Park. Custer County dispatch received a 911 call Monday, May 18 at 1:44 p.m. from a male reporting his wife had been rammed by a buffalo and was seriously injured. According to Custer County Sheriff Marty Mechaley and Lt. Derrick Reifenrath, the woman and her husband were walking south on Grace Coolidge Trail near Center Lake when they encountered around five bulls an estimated 1,500 feet ahead of them. The bulls continued down the trail ahead of the couple and out of sight.

title: Eight Republicans in crowded commission field
description: A crowded field of Republicans will head into the June 2 election looking to take a seat as a Custer County Commissioner, with three seats available. The Primary Election will determine which candidates take their seats as commissioners next January, as there are no Democrats or Independents entered in the race. Mike Linde Among the candidates is Mike Linde, an incumbent who has served eight years on the commission and seeks a third and final term.

title: Three seek a pair of Hermosa seats
description: Three candidates are vying for a pair of three-year terms on the Hermosa Town Board in the June 2 election. Kel Koontz currently serves as the chair of the Hermosa Board of Trustees, and has served on the Board for two and a half years. He has lived in Hermosa for five years, and got involved in Hermosa’s politics out of interest in the town’s infrastructure. “I wanted to find out what was the actual state of the town infrastructure,” he said.

title: Hermosa to vote on two resolutions
description: Two resolutions passed by the Hermosa Board of Trustees were put to a vote during the June 2 election through a petition process by the citizens. Resolution 2026-01 is in regards to creating the Tax Increment Finance District (TIF) No. 2 on the west side of Hwy. 79, and Resolution 2026-05 is in regards to the State Revolving Fund (SRF) Loan and revenue bond that would fund the drilling of a new Madison well and other improvements to the drinking water system, including treatment for Hermosa’s existing wells.

title: Elk Mountain board seats up for election
description: In the Elk Mountain School District, two board of education seats currently held by Jason Bradeen and Kevin Rosse are up for election. The seats are for three-year terms. Bradeen and Rosse filed petitions, as did Terri Janssen. The primary election is Tuesday, June 2. Janssen is a part-time paralegal. She purchased property in Custer County eight or nine years ago and officially moved in December of 2020 after retiring.

title: Wells, Jensen face off in Buffalo Gap
description: Herman Wells is facing Steve Jensen in the race for a seat on the Buffalo Gap Town Board in the June 2 election. Wells has been a resident of Buffalo Gap for just over three and a half years. His military career and subsequent service with the Department of Defense have taken him across the country and the world, and he says that has given him a “unique perspective into working with and becoming involved in new communities and the different perspectives of the people residing in those communities.”

title: Town discusses proposed project
Bridge getting replaced after long wait
Mueller, Bush vie for District 1 commission
Candidate forum gives glimpse of those running
Primary election set for Tuesday
description: Don’t forget to vote next week. The primary election is Tuesday, June 2, and polls are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Sample ballots were published in the May 20 issue of the Custer County Chronicle. The City of Custer will not hold an election this year since the candidates for the three two-year council seats were uncontested. Dixie Whitaker ran for Ward I, Julie Jenniges ran for Ward II and Monica McGowan ran for Ward III.

title: County approves variance despite opposition
A look at who is on the ballot
Concerns addressed over speed in town
City, county may reopen LEO talks
description: Negotiations for a new law enforcement contract between Custer County and the City of Custer are likely to resume in some form or fashion in the near future. Exactly how they will unfold is not set in stone, however. At the May 13 meeting of the Custer County Commission the commission discussed its push to have a joint, public meeting with the Custer City Council to discuss the issue and bring the public into the fold as to how the negotiations have transpired and how they did or did not come together.

title: School board celebrates good news, progress
Uranium drilling hearings open in Hot Springs
description: By Meghan O’Brien South Dakota Searchlight

title: School budget decreased by 12.48 percent
description: At the budget hearing May 11 in the Custer board room, the Custer School District Board of Education reviewed a total proposed budget for Fiscal Year (FY) 27, seeing an overall decrease of 12.48 percent in comparison to FY 26. Excluding the Career and Technical Education (CTE) building expenses, FY 26 budget was $19,068,856, and the preliminary budget for FY 27 is $16,688,702. The CTE building numbers were excluded because “we want to compare real numbers from real spending, not building spending year-to-year,” said business manager Sarah Wedge.

title: Hayward area structure fire escalates to two alarms
Widow of Vietnam War veteran encourages more nominees
Board of Regents ‘leaning in’ to AI use
City continues sidewalks research
description: Two weeks after sending the issue to a pair of committees, the Custer City Council sent a sidewalk issue to another of its committees, seeking more time and research before making a decision that will impact when and where sidewalks will need to be installed in new developments.

title: Council sets stiff fines for merchandise displays
Incumbents sweep city races
Forest service, state agree to work together on forest management
Tour dates announced for One Book South Dakota
Mechaley, Hindle, Sorenson win commission seats
description: The Custer County Commission will have a new face, a relatively new face, and a familiar face come January. Incumbent Craig Hindle retained his seat on the commission during yesterday’s Primary Election, and will be joined by current but soon-to-be-retired Custer County Sheriff Marty Mechaley on the commission, along with former commissioner Jesse Sorenson. Mechaley was the top vote-getter, with 1,263 votes, while Hindle had 840 votes. Sorenson pulled in 823 votes. The three will serve a four-year term.

title: County to lay ground work for new tax
description: As soon as Jan. 1, Custer County could implement the new half cent sales tax counties are now able to charge thanks to Senate Bill 96, which was passed during the 2026 legislative session. The Custer County Commission listened to an overview of how the implementation will work from commission legal counsel Aaron Davis at the commission’s May 27 meeting, after having asked Davis to research the issue at the commission’s previous meeting.

title: City asked to deny transient permit
description: Three businessmen—including one from Hill City—came before the Custer City Council at the council’s May 18 meeting to request the council deny a transient merchant permit for the property at 544 Mt. Rushmore Rd. The property is a lot sandwiched between Horatio’s Homemade Ice Cream and Custer Senior Center. It is owned by Khiljee Realty, LLC, and annually hosts a tent that typically sets up early-to-mid July and remains open through the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally.

title: District partners with YMCA for early education
description: Beginning in the fall of 2026, the Custer School District (CSD) and the Custer YMCA are coming together to create a seamless early learning experience that helps children feel confident, supported and ready for kindergarten. This was announced at the Board of Education meeting in Custer May 11.

title: Balciunas sentenced to five years
description: The man who in February was held at gunpoint during a burglary attempt was sentenced to five years in the South Dakota State Penitentiary for the act. Darius Balciunas, 38, was sentenced in Seventh Judicial Circuit Court by judge Heidi Linngren, who in sentencing Balciunas noted the increasing nature and degree of violence in his crimes. Balciunas is known to law enforcement in the area for a variety of offenses, which until now were of the petty or misdemeanor variety, including drivers license issues, traffic issues and simple assault.

title: Fall River Health Services contributing to housing
description: In a first-of-its-kind project in South Dakota, the small hospital in Hot Springs is investing in a subdivision project to provide housing for its employees. Fall River Health Services, an independent nonprofit medical center is paying $2.3 million of the overall $3.4 million cost of infrastructure for a subdivision that could create 48 new affordable housing units a few hundred yards from the hospital campus.

title: Road issues brought forward
description: Road issues—or one stretch of road in particular—were front and center at the June 4 meeting of the Custer County Commission, as the commission listened to three people air road concerns during the open forum portion of the meeting. John Gisi, who lives off 20 Mile/Remington Road, said he had concerns over a stretch of Remington Road that was having its ditches pulled in, saying a long stretch of it was “barely passable for a pickup.”

title: Buffalo involved in CSP attack relocated
description: The Custer State Park buffalo bull that was recently involved in the death of a Canadian tourist will live out the rest of its days in the custody of the Rosebud Sioux Tribe, it was announced last week. “The Rosebud Sioux Tribe has stepped forward to take possession of the bison, ensuring that the animal will not be euthanized,” Rosebud Sioux Tribe Game, Fish and Parks said in a press release. “Instead, he will be safely relocated where he will be able to live out the remainder of his natural life in a secure environment away from the public.”

title: School district contemplates drivers ed
description: Custer School District eighth graders, don’t start your engines. At least, not yet. At the June 8 meeting of the Custer School District Board of Education in Hermosa, the board of education held a preliminary discussion of the pros and cons of a possible driver’s education course that, if implemented, would be offered to school district eighth graders. Potential obstacles—such as the cost of instruction and when to schedule such a course—were discussed, along with the obvious benefits of children learning to drive safely and the ability to get licenses earlier.

title: Fire code confusion
Agency assessing water for PFAS
School board finishes out fiscal year
Volksmarch celebrates 40 years
description: Forty years and thousands of miles later, the Crazy Horse Volksmarch is still going strong. Last Saturday marked the 40th rendition of the Crazy Horse Spring Volksmarch, and two days prior to the march itself a group of Crazy Horse, American Volkssport Association (AVA) and its Black Hills Chapter celebrated the 40th anniversary with a press conference, reception and fellowship at  Laughing Water Restaurant at Crazy Horse Memorial.

title: Fine Artists Festival coming June 19-20
description: Join some of the finest artists in the Black Hills for a weekend festival on the lawn at Sixth and Washington Street in Custer. The Fine Artists Festival is returning for its second year June 19-20 from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. and will feature around 29 artists and their work. The festival is run and organized by Deeda Cordin, a photographer and owner of Deep Creek Gallery in Custer. Cordin grew up on cattle ranches in New Mexico and Wyoming and was homeschooled until her freshman year of high school.

title: Council settles sidewalk issue
description: After a pair of council meetings and three committee meetings, a decision has been reached: sidewalks will not be required along Park Avenue as the lots there are developed. That was the decision rendered by the Custer City Council at the council’s June 1 meeting, although the final decision didn’t come before plenty of discussion and changing of minds as the discussion unfolded.

title: Mining opponent files federal lawsuit
description: The status of a hearing on an exploratory uranium drilling permit was left uncertain after a state board adjourned until further notice, following a private session to discuss legal matters. The permit application is from Clean Nuclear Energy Corporation, which is seeking to drill dozens of holes up to 700 feet deep on state land. The proposed site is near the rim of Craven Canyon in South Dakota’s southern Black Hills.

title: Forest Service debuts rec app
description: To kick off Great Outdoors Month the U.S. Forest Service is launching a new, single visitor-information mobile app, National Forests and Grasslands, now available for download as visitors plan their summer trips to recreation sites across the national forest system. For the first time the app provides the most complete and accurate collection of Forest Service recreation sites that has ever been made available to the public, along with important planning tools like critical safety alerts, closures, amenity details and more.

title: Town firework plans
Trail master plan takes shape
Mining opponent files federal lawsuit
Derrick Reifenrath appointed sheriff
description: There’s a new sheriff in town. Derrick Reifenrath of the Custer County Sheriff’s Office was appointed as sheriff June 18 due to the retirement of Sheriff Marty Mechaley. Reifenrath ran uncontested for the position of Custer County Sheriff when petitions were open this spring. The appointment took place at a special meeting of the Custer County Commission Thursday in the commission meeting room. “Thank you, gentlemen, for all the years. I really appreciate all of you,” said Mechaley. The commissioners said they appreciated Mechaley as well.

title: Besco alleged to have embezzled more than $131,000
description: The Buffalo Gap Town Board convened June 9 for a special meeting to hear a report presented by state auditor general Russ Olson regarding alleged embezzlement of funds by the former town finance officer, Heather Jean Besco (a.k.a. Heather Jean Besco-Clyde) to the tune of more than $131,000 from 2016-24. She was arrested in Nebraska April 9 and charged in Seventh Judicial Circuit Court for Grand Theft-Embezzlement of Property Received in Trust.

title: School board hears facilities update
description: The Custer High School serving kitchen is in need of upgrades, and time is short to get them done. At the June 8 meeting of the Custer School District Board of Education, the board discussed changes to the kitchen that are required by the state’s Deparment of Health, including upgraded wall panels, sink and countertops. The needs were part of the district’s Facilities and Transportation Committee discussion that was held prior to the board’s regular meeting, which was held at the Hermosa School.

title: Funding request sent to committee
description: The Custer Volunteer Fire Department’s 2026 additional funding request was sent to the Public Works Committee for further discussion. This was decided at the June 15 meeting of the Custer City Council. Councilperson Nina Nielsen made the motion, and it was unanimously approved without further discussion.

title: County approve Black Hills Marketplace TIF
Keystone gets gaga pit, hears summer updates
Fall River Health Services contributing to housing
Trump, fireworks at Mount Rushmore
description: President Donald Trump will attend the first fireworks display in six years at Mount Rushmore National Memorial July 3, according to announcements last Thursday from Freedom 250 and South Dakota Republican Gov. Larry Rhoden.

title: Mechaleys guests at ‘Igniting Hope’
description: It’s been over six years since an awkward group of now-former Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints (FLDS) girls first reached out to now-former Custer County Sheriff Marty Mechaley with the goal of leaving the FLDS. Fast forward to today, and Mechaley is recently retired, and those once-naive girls—daughters and a niece of self-proclaimed prophet of the FLDS Warren Jeffs—are now mothers, employees and thriving outside of the constraints of the FLDS.

title: County waiting on numbers for HVAC system
description: The Custer County Courthouse’s aging and increasingly obsolete heating and cooling system was among the items discussed at the June 24 meeting of the Custer County Commission, with county maintenance supervisor Joe Panza reporting on a pair of meetings he had with Witt’s Heating & Air Conditioning and JAM Heating & Cooling soliciting advice on how to deal with the courthouse system.

title: Trump will attend July 3 Mount Rushmore fireworks
City accepts bid, declines alternates
BID tax increase proposal draws discussion
Petition fails to gather enough signatures
Independence Day travel could reach record levels
‘They just won’t listen:’ Rural SD nears postal breaking point
Old Time Country Fourth events start Thursday
description: The Custer Area Chamber of Commerce invites residents and visitors to celebrate Independence Day in the heart of the Black Hills with Custer’s Old Time Country Fourth of July Celebration. This year’s festivities are especially meaningful as communities across the nation commemorate America’s 250th anniversary with a weekend filled with patriotism, family fun, live music, parades and fireworks. Festivities begin on Thursday, July 2, with a free Patriotic Story Time at 10 a.m. at the 1881 Courthouse Museum.

title: City sends new LEO proposal to county
description: A new proposal from the City of Custer would see the city pay Custer County $600,000 a year for the next five years to have the Custer County Sheriff’s Office provide law enforcement services in the city once more. The proposal, which will be sent in letter form to the county, was unanimously approved by the council following an executive session at the council’s July 6 meeting. The proposal would see the full $600,000 begin Jan. 1, while the remainder of 2026 would be for a prorated amount.

title: Rapid City man dies in crash near Hermosa
description: An 18-year-old Rapid City man died in a two-vehicle crash July 1 near Hermosa. Preliminary crash information indicates Carlos Ray Cross, the driver of a 2019 Toyota Camry, was traveling westbound on South Dakota Hwy. 40 at 5:54 p.m. two miles east of Hermosa when he entered the eastbound lane. At the same time, the driver of a 2021 Ford Explorer, driven by Alicia Nicole Hayden of Hermosa, 35, approached the Camry from the eastbound lanes and tried to avoid a collision. The vehicles struck each other.

title: County begins budget process
Trump delivers July 4 address
Rock strike adds days to project
Lightning strikes (at least) twice in Custer
description: What are the odds of lightning striking twice in Custer three blocks apart? On the evening of July 7, random chance became a reality as St. John the Baptist Parish Center and a private residence were hit by lightning. Administrative officer and firefighter for the Custer Volunteer Fire Department (CVFD) Selena Spring, said the department responded to both incidents.

title: Custer set to get new events center
description: A new events center is in the works in Custer, and will be located on the Hwy. 16 frontage at Buffalo Ridge Camp Resort. Mike and Bonnie Tennyson, owner of Custer Hospitality, which owns the camp resort and  five hotel properties around Custer, floated the idea of an events center at the July 6 meeting of the Custer City Council. He is proposing to fund the project through creation of a Business Improvement District (BID).

title: County discusses ambulances, alternative energy
1880 Train goes off track in Keystone
Pennington county responds to cyber incident
Another goring in Custer State Park
South Dakota T. rex fetches $50 million at auction
School board turns over seat to Holcomb
Aldermen create board to look into new tax
Water concerns force shut down
Surge in advance voting for Republican runoff driven by party switchers, county auditors say
Holly Nielsen’s FCCLA project first in nation
description: From bronze to gold, Holly Nielsen is making herself known in the Family, Career and Community Leaders of America (FCCLA) organization nationwide, placing first at the FCCLA National Leadership Conference July 6-10 in the National Programs in Action—Stand Up category for her project Petals of Appreciation. Nielsen, the daughter of Dane and Karen Nielsen of Custer, is heading into her senior year at Custer Jr./Sr. High School, and she has been involved in FCCLA since seventh grade.

title: GDD event results listed
description: Winners at the annual Gold Discovery Days are as follows: Bob Plaisted Memorial Car Show Best of Show Car Stock—65 Chevy Impalass by Duane Schuh. Best of Show Car Modified—1927 Ford T-Roadster by Duane Wamsley. Best of Show Truck Stock—1933 Dodge Model HC by Terry and Jean Downing. Best of Show Truck Modified—1972 GMC by Mike Peacock. Best of Show Convertible—1969 Bobbi Scott-Hindle. Best of Show in Progress—1951 Ford F1 Panel Van by Wayne Davis. Mayor’s Choice—1956 F100 by Tom Hofer.

title: Answers sought over subdivision
description: More subdividing of land in Big Medicine Subdivision northwest of Custer has some residents concerned, with a handful of them attending the July 8 meeting of the Custer County Commission to express those concerns. John Parker, owner of 50 acres of land in the area, has submitted a plan that would see him subdivide the land to presumably sell as around five acre parcels. County ordinance states a home cannot be built on under one acre of land.

title: Parade mural canceled, both parties share their side
description: What’s going on with the mural on the north wall of Lynn’s Dakotamart? There was a mural being painted, then it was covered up and now a completely different mural is being painted. Originally, the Custer County Historical Society had a contract with artist Taylor Young to paint a mural. However, in what was described as an unfortunate turn of events, the scene was returned to a blank slate when the contract was terminated June 24. Both parties have since shared their side of the story with the Chronicle.

title: Confusion abounds on road, plat issue
description: “At this point I just need to know what you’re going to require me to do.” Those were the words of east Custer County property owner Brandi Hunsaker, who was before the Custer County Commission at the commission’s July 8 meeting to address confusion over when and if she was to upgrade the section line on South Fairburn Road as it enters into Hunsaker Subdivision. “As far as we know, we are not going to request (Hunsaker) to improve it,” commission chairman Jim Lintz said.

title: New term, same team for Custer School District
description: Business shall continue as usual in the Custer School District (CSD) as Larry Baker, Travis Hartshorn and Sara Barrick took their oath of office to continue as members of the board of education for the next three years at the July 13 meeting in Custer. Baker and Hartshorn also asked to forgo payment for their services.

title: County budget taking shape
County nearly up and running
New interchange proposed for Catron, Hwy. 16
City, county inching closer to law enforcement pact
description: Judging by events that took place at the July 22 meeting of the Custer County Commission, it appears the City of Custer and Custer County may be nearing reaching an agreement on a new contract for the county to provide law enforcement for the City of Custer once more. Nothing is a done deal yet, however, as a proposed requirement for the contract received by Custer County in its most recent letter from the City of Custer has provided the latest sticking point in the negotiations.

title: City wants more info from CVFD
description: The Custer City Council wants to see more details of budget figures from the Custer Volunteer Fire Department before agreeing to provide an additional $269,500 in funding to the $30,5000 allocated to the department for 2026. That was the message relayed to department chief Matt Spring at the July 20 meeting of the council, at which Spring came before the department to make the request for the additional funding.

title: Hermosa battles water supply issues
description: After weeks of setbacks and water restrictions, the Hermosa Board of Trustees has mapped out a way forward to preserve and strengthen the drinking water supply to Hermosa residents. The timing of the ordeal coincided with record-setting regional heat and drought conditions, but an end is in sight.

title: Burn ban back on
description: Custer County has reinstated a burn ban effective as of Monday, to coincide with the Black Hills National Forest moving to Level II restrictions on Forest Service land.

title: Woman dies in Hermosa house fire
description: While on the phone with emergency services July 21, 77-year-old Margaret Miracle of Hermosa died of smoke inhalation due to the fire that consumed her home and blocked the exit. The fire was called into the Custer County Sheriff’s Office’s 911 center by Miracle who was trapped inside at 7:45 p.m. The house was located off Hwy. 36. “(Miracle) reported that there was a fire in her living room and that she was unable to get out of the house,” said Custer County Sheriff Derrick Reifenrath.

title: Trump says no August recess with out SAVE America Act
description: President Donald Trump on Monday called on the U.S. Senate to cancel its five-week August break, keeping lawmakers in session to advance several of his priorities, despite not having the votes. Trump wrote in a social media post that he wanted Senate Majority Leader John Thune to keep the chamber open, preventing vulnerable Republicans facing reelection from the campaign trail, to pass a voter identification bill, among other measures.

title: SAR in the running for $30k prize
description: Friends of Custer County Search and Rescue (Friends) has been selected as one of only five North American finalists in the Search, Rescue & Emergency Support Services category of the 2026 Defender Service Awards presented by CHASE.

title: Citizens hear ideas on potential additional tax
Tragedy strikes at Hippie Hole
County budget passes for now
Miner airs concerns about surcharges
Fire restrictions in national forest
Museum switching tracks as new owner detours lease
Big paydays result from $50M auction of SD T. rex skeleton
County fair starts Thursday
description: Mosey on over to Hermosa this week for the 2026 Custer County Fair Aug. 6-9. This year’s fair is dedicated to Jim and Brenda Lintz who have been staples in the Custer County community, operating a small century ranch just west of Hermosa that has been in the family for over 120 years. Jim has been a fixture in the Hermosa volunteer fire department as an EMT, served several years in Pierre in legislature as well as being a Custer County Commissioner and on numerous boards, including the Custer County Fair Board to help promote and support the ranching cattle industry.

title: County approves Big Medicine plat
description: The final plat that will create 10 lots roughly five acres in size in the Big Medicine Subdivision was unanimously approved by the Custer County Commission at the commission’s July 22 meeting, but not without both concerns and protest from those who live in the area of the subdivision. The applicant, John Parker, plans to subdivide 50 acres of land into 10 lots, with access to the lots coming from Renegade Pass and/or War Bonnet Road. The subdivision is located northwest of the City of Custer.

title: Wickre sentenced to 10 years
description: A Colorado man was sentenced to 10 years in prison earlier this month after pleading guilty to grand theft for accepting approximately $124,000 that was to be used toward building a Custer County resident a home, but instead spending all the money and never doing anything toward the construction.

title: CSD libraries receive statewide award
description: Here’s an achievement to bookmark. The Custer School District (CSD) libraries, including Custer Elementary School, Custer High School and Hermosa School, recently received the School Achievement Through Libraries (SATL) award through the South Dakota State Library (SDSL). This accreditation is valid for three years, running from 2026-2029. The application process for the award was completed by district library coordinator Doris Ann Mertz and her team of library paras. Mertz was the county library director for 11 years before she transitioned to  CSD in 2022.

title: Fatal crash near Hill City
description: The South Dakota Highway Patrol has officially identified the two people who died in a three-vehicle crash Thursday near Hill City. Authorities say Kurt D. Klokkenga and Regina Klokkenga, both of Emden, Ill., were killed in the crash on Hwy. 385 near mile marker 89. According to preliminary information, Kurt Klokkenga and Kendall D. Klokkenga were traveling northbound on separate Harley-Davidson motorcycles when they approached a Toyota 4Runner that was stopped in the roadway, waiting to turn onto Wrinkle Valley Road.

title: Honoring educational perseverance
description: A new memorial scholarship has been established in loving memory of a local Hill City man honoring his extraordinary perseverance throughout his educational journey and inspiring others to find an educational pathway that leads to success. The Go Far Foundation announced the launch of the Spencer Coy Sandven Memorial Perseverance Scholarship July 10 on its Facebook page, stating, “This scholarship isn’t just about grades—it’s about recognizing young people who have overcome challenges, kept moving forward and continue to make a positive impact.”

title: Time ticking down to run for trustee
description: Those hoping to run for the Keystone Town Board of Trustees have until Aug. 18 at 5 p.m. to file a petition with the finance officer. The deadline is a week earlier than originally explained, due to an error with the election calendar put out by the Secretary of State. There are two seats open on the board. Trustees approved a not to exceed $9,000 survey task order at the Aug. 5 meeting. The projects will determine the location of the water and sewer mains relative to property boundaries, rights of way and easements for the  Presidential Hospitality property.

title: Work session shows state of projects
description: The Hill City Common Council (HCCC) held a work session Aug. 6 at city hall to discuss water and sewer infrastructure projects. Mayor Tana Nichols  began the evening by telling the audience how hard officials have been working on the projects. This was evident as all city officials were present including city administrator Nate Anderson joining the meeting via phone and the city finance officer and director of public works in attendance. HCCC president Ethan Walker led the meeting with a slide show and packet that illustrated the predicaments before the council.

title: Open house shares vision of Hwy. 16 corridor
description: The South Dakota Department of Transportation (SDDOT) hosted an open house explaining its plans for the Hwy. 16 corridor. The meeting Aug. 4 was held in two rooms, one in which a looped video explained the project and another where some SDDOT engineers were on hand explaining the project.

title: New Keystone event to bring people together
description: A new event is being held Aug. 21-22 in Keystone featuring a parade, street dance and an old fashioned community picnic. Rushmore Heritage Days is the brainchild of Sandi Mclain who together with a host of volunteers has been hard at work since March to create a celebration for the nation’s 250th birthday. The Rushmore Heritage Days is a celebration of heritage, mining, agriculture and Native Americans. The event kicks off Aug. 21 at 11 a.m. with a parade starting at the Keystone Mall and ending at the Keystone Community Center.

title: Back to school for CSD Aug. 25
description: By Esther Noe

title: Three-wheel cycles becoming hot ride
description: It takes only a brief drive through the streets of Sturgis during the 2026 motorcycle rally to realize that three-wheeled cycles have become a hot new trend in the biker world. Motorcycles with three wheels instead of two can readily be seen driving in traffic, parked amid the rows of bikes on Main Street or displayed at temporary sales and rental lots that pop up during the Sturgis rally that attracts more than 500,000 bikers to South Dakota each August.

title: Council gets West Dam update
description: As phase three of the West Dam reconstruction project—the construction of the dam itself—moves ahead, phase two of the construction—removal of sediment from the reservoir, modifications around the ninth green at Rocky Knolls Golf Course and some grading work—is winding to a close.

title: Honoring heroes
description: One of the nation’s most recognizable tributes to those who served in Vietnam will arrive in Newcastle this week, giving residents and visitors an opportunity to honor the more than 58,000 Americans who never returned home while also celebrating the service and sacrifice of Vietnam veterans. The wall made a stop in Custer yesterday.

title: BHE seeks surcharge for new station
description: Black Hills Energy (BHE) has provided an update on its Lange II Generating Station, a new 99-megawatt natural gas-fired electric power facility under construction in Rapid City. With state-of-the-art gas turbine technology, BHE officials say Lange II will meet growing power demand from current Black Hills Energy residential and commercial customers following the planned retirement next year of the 1960s-era Ben French Power Plant.

title: Mitchell baseball libel lawsuit dismissed
description: More than a year after the case by a former Mitchell baseball player was filed, a judge has ruled that statements made by the American Legion and circulated by the Mitchell Republic and KELO-TV do not constitute defamation. A South Dakota judge has ruled in favor of the American Legion and two media companies in a defamation lawsuit filed by a former Mitchell baseball player.

title: State rally fatality count officially three
description: The State of South Dakota’s Department of Public Safety lists three as of Monday as the number of those who died district-wide as a result of Sturgis Motorcycle Rally-related accidents. Last year there were two such fatalities. However, this does not take into account four deaths prior to the official start of the Rally that involved motorcycle accidents. Below is a summary of all fatal accidents or accidents that happened in the area from Aug. 8 to Aug. 11 of the rally.

title: Back to school for the Rangers
Alderman say no to extra height
School maintenance team paves the way
Trustee resigns as town talks budget
Deerfield crash victim ID’d
South Dakota taxpayers spend millions on  cyberattacks after federal grant rejected
City OKs LEO contract
description: Thirteen months after negotiations began, the City of Custer and Custer County have agreed on a new contract and will see the Custer County Sheriff’s Office resume providing law enforcement services to the city.

title: Rally numbers see sharp drop
description: Numbers were down across the board for this year’s Sturgis Motorcycle Rally, as anecdotal stories and hard numbers tell the story of a rally that saw a dip in visitation from last year’s 85th rally. The South Dakota Department of Transportation said overall traffic count at the nine locations enterering Sturgis was down 10 percent overall, with a total of 448,166 vehicles entering over the course of the official 10 days of the rally. That number is off the previous five-year average for 10 days, which is 498,042 vehicles.

title: Custer psychologist facing charges
description: A Custer County psychologist is facing criminal charges on allegations he engaged in sexual acvitity with a patient. Stephen Stuart Greene, 69, faces charges of sexual penetration by a psychotherapist, a Class 4 Felony, as well as sexual contact by a psychoterapist, a Class 5 Felony. Class 4 felonies are punishable by up to 10 years in prison and/or a $20,000 fine, while a Class 5 Felony is punishable by up to five years in prison and/or a $10,000 fine.

title: Fireworks cost more than it generated
description: The fireworks display last month at Mount Rushmore cost the state of South Dakota $450,000 more than the event generated in economic impact, according to the state Department of Tourism. The state spent $2.8 million to plan and produce the July 3 celebration, which generated $2.35 million of economic impact, the department said in a Monday press release. The department attributed the economic analysis to the research firm Tourism Economics.

title: Bike wreck claims one
description: A Connecticut man died last Monday in a single-vehicle crash near Custer. Preliminary crash information indicates Robert Thomas Ryan, the driver of a 2002 Yamaha Super Hawk, was traveling westbound on Hwy. 16A near mile marker 27. Ryan became separated from his motorcycle when the Yamaha left the roadway, entered the westbound ditch and overturned. He sustained fatal injuries. The investigation is ongoing. All information released is preliminary.

title: Changes implemented at Harlow’s
description: Changes are coming to Harlow’s School Bus Service for the 2026-27 school year, including updated bus tags for backpacks, cleaning schedules and regular maintenance from a third-party company. Harlow’s location manager for the Custer School District (CSD) Kelli Werlinger attended the board of education meeting in Hermosa Aug. 10 to share more about the updates in services. First is an increase in accountability for drivers. Werlinger said she holds drivers very accountable and addresses concerns or complaints immediately.

title: No new fatalities as rally wraps up
description: The State of South Dakota’s Department of Public Safety lists three as the number of those who died district-wide as a result of Sturgis Motorcycle Rally-related accidents. Last year there were also three such fatalities. Below is a summary of all fata accidents that happened in the area from Aug. 11-16 of the rally. There were no new fatal accidents since last week’s update story.

title: Citizen demands transparency in Keystone
District welcomes new teachers
description: School is back in session, and three new teachers are at the helm, along with a paraprofessional who achieved her teacher certification. Nora Smolnisky is the seventh and eighth grade English Language Arts teacher at Custer Jr./Sr. High School (CHS). “What I enjoy most is helping students learn how clear and effective communication and strong thinking relate to their lives both now and after formal schooling,” said Smolnisky. Originally from Worthington, Minn., Smolnisky lived in Sioux Falls and Izmir, Turkey before settling in Custer almost 10 years ago.

title: County fire ban still in effect
description: Yes, Custer County has received some rain recently. No, that doesn’t mean the county fire ban has been lifted. At the Aug. 12 meeting of the Custer County Commission county emergency management director Steve Esser said he had received inquiries as to the removal of the fire ban after the recent rains, but reminded those in attendance the fire ban is still very much in place and that he was “not seeing it (removing the ban) anywhere in the near future.”

title: County balks at road agreement
description: As of now, Custer County does not have an agreement with the U.S. Forest Service to maintain roughly 168 miles of the over 400 miles of roadway in the county. Those 168 miles—U.S. Forest Service roads that the county has long maintained under what is known as a Schedule A agreement—are not going to be abandoned by the county, however; there just won’t be existing obligations put on the county that were required under the Schedule A agreement.

title: Done just in time
description: It’s been clear for some time that the Quonset, which was moved to the Custer County Fairgrounds from Rapid City in 1967, needed to be replaced. However, the process was sped up due to hail damage received a few years ago. “The cash value wasn’t very high on the building, so they (the insurance company) would give us double the amount of what they were going to give us if we replaced the building. So that was what sprung it into motion a lot faster than we had planned,” said president of the Custer County Fair Board Greg Neugebauer.

title: Committee seeks three Habitat builds
description: When Gene Fennell discussed being on the new steering committee for Habitat for Humanity in Custer with local realtor  Andrea Ronning, she knew she wanted to help. However, she also wanted to make sure something got done. “I didn’t want to (just) be on another housing board. We’ve all sat on these boards, we’ve all had these conversations in town,” she said. “There’s not one thing that has been built. That’s why I’m so grateful for this steering committee. We all jumped in, working our tails off to get something done.”

title: Man arrested for fighting deputy
description: A 40-year-old Fort Morgan, Colo., man is facing a felony charge of Simple Assault against a Law Enforcement Officer, as well as four misdemeanor charges in relation to an incident with a Custer County Sheriff’s Office deputy Aug. 13.

title: More fire ban talk at county meeting
description: More county fire ban exemptions were granted at the Aug. 26 meeting of the Custer County Commission, while a question was raised as to whether or not incinerators are permitted under the ban as well.

title: Nonprofit strives to be PALS to veterans
description: A local nonprofit organization is endeavoring to be PALS to veterans at the Hot Springs VA Medical Center and the Michael J. Fitzmaurice South Dakota State Veterans Home. PALS’, or the Patriotic Alliance of Loyal Service’s, mission is to make a better community for veterans and their families by working to assist other veteran organizations in filling the gap for needs.

title: BHE now seeks both rate increase, surcharge
Hill City takes the top spot West River
More discussion on subsidizing rates
SD postal problems largely unchanged as Congress weighs legislation
Dry winter to blame
description: Custer is behind on precipitation, but it’s winter—not summer—that is mostly to blame

title: Custer roots lead Rapid City public information
description: With roots reaching back to Custer, Tessa Jaeger and Brendyn Medina are at the helm of community relations in Rapid City, serving as the Public Information Officers (PIOs) for the fire department and police department, respectively. Jaeger was born and raised in Rapid City and visited Custer often growing up since both her parents used to live in Custer, as did all of her grandparents.

title: 250th exhibit traces state history
description: The Great American State Fair was held from June 25 through July 10 at the National Mall in Washington, D.C. The event spanned from the Capitol to the Washington Monument and had exhibits, live music, a ferris wheel, a rodeo and exhibits from states and territories.

title: Keystone citizens make accusations to board
How donors in De Smet are bringing big projects to little town on the prairie
